extractor.note: Partial pass over § 37, its Beilage XXI, and § 1 of the Amsterdam Lectures, where the psychological and transcendental reductions are distinguished.

coverage_note: Covers § 37 of the Systematic Part, Beilage XXI to § 37, and § 1 of 'Transcendental Phenomenology Over Against Psychological Phenomenology'. § 3f, § 4, § 45 and the remaining sections carrying hits are not covered.

units.claim: The reduction is formulated as the method by which the immanent, pure subjectivity, is unveiled as a field of scientific investigation.
units.quote: Husserl now formulates the *method of phenomenological reduction* as the method by which the *immanent* — pure subjectivity — is unveiled as a field of scientific investigation.

units.claim: The phenomenological-psychological reduction remains within the natural attitude and brackets world-positing only in order to attend to the intentional structures of psychic life.
units.quote: The phenomenological-psychological reduction, by contrast, *remains within the natural attitude* — it remains a science of *psychic* subjectivity within the world — but *brackets the world-positing* in order to attend purely to the *intentional structures* of psychic life.

units.claim: The bracketing suspends rather than denies or doubts the natural positing, shifting the interest from the being of the perceived to the structure of perceiving and the perceived as meant.
units.quote: This bracketing is methodological — a *change of theoretical interest*, not a metaphysical conversion.

units.claim: Both reductions are bracketings, but the psychological one brackets world-positing while remaining in the natural attitude and the transcendental one brackets the being of the world altogether.
units.quote: The *transcendental* reduction brackets the *being of the world altogether* and turns to *transcendental subjectivity* as the *absolute ground* of all positing.

units.claim: The psychological reduction is easier to motivate and opens the field of intentional life, after which the transcendental reduction can be carried out as a further radicalization.
units.quote: Once this field is clear, the *transcendental* reduction can be carried out as a *further radicalization* of the bracketing.

units.claim: Transcendental and psychological phenomenology pass into one another through a mere alteration of attitude, the same phenomena appearing with different signs that fundamentally alter their sense.
units.quote: so that on both sides "the same" phenomena and essential insights appear, but, so to speak, with *different signs* that *fundamentally alter their sense*

units.claim: Even the pure psychology delimited by the psychological-phenomenological reduction remains positive science with the world as pre-given ground, and is itself transcendentally problematic.
units.quote: Even the phenomenologically pure psychology — thematically delimited by the *psychological-phenomenological reduction* — is still *positive science*; it has the world as *pre-given ground*.

units.claim: Transcendental philosophy requires a fully universal phenomenological reduction exercising epoche over the entire experiential world and all positive sciences, transforming them into transcendental phenomena.
units.quote: an *extended and fully universal phenomenological reduction* is required — the *transcendental* one — which does justice to the *universality of the problem* and exercises *epoche* with regard to the *entire experiential world*

units.claim: Descartes already touched on this reduction by setting the being of the whole experiential world out of play and recognizing that the ego cogito as universum of pure subjectivity remains.
units.quote: Already Descartes had touched on this reduction, insofar as he set out of play (by his methodical principle of *epoche* with regard to all that could possibly be doubted) the *being of the whole experiential world*.
